items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Simeon, myself, Don Kirkpatrick, Freddie Moore, we all sit there and listened.

ctx.x: argument, and Wilbur went on... They almost come to blows. And then after that, everybody stopped. Simeon, myself, Don Kirkpatrick, Freddie Moore, we all sit there and listened. And they went through the whole thing. "Well, you left Mama when we needed you. We was on the road, and you left us and went to school." On and on like that.
They took you all through that, huh.

items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: Then in May of 1951, Conrad Janis, Dick Smith, Tom Sharpstein, Danny Barker was playing guitar

ctx.x: Let's see. I don't think "Down By The Riverside" is listed here. But there's "Tiger Rag," there's "Yellow Dog Blues," "Bugle Boy March," "Kansas City Stomps," and there's a whole list of things -- "1919 March" is one of them. Then in May of 1951, Conrad Janis, Dick Smith, Tom Sharpstein, Danny Barker was playing guitar, apparently there was no bass player, but Elmer Shobel(?) was playing piano replacing Bob Green. Do you remember that date in New York?
